chapter: Steamer Capitol and New Orleans bands
title: Other clarinetists and trombonists he heard
summary: Asked about clarinetists, he recalls Big Eye Louis, George Lewis, Willie Humphrey, Peter Bocage, and Jim Robinson; the block ends in ASR looping.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Who were some of the other clarinetists you heard when you were a small boy? You mentioned Piku. Can you think of any others? Do you remember Big Eye Louis for instance? Louis DeLille was his real name.
Louis DeLille? Yes. I remember him very well. Big Eye Louis.

Yeah, I used to hear him in those walking parades. And I used to hear this George Lewis too when he won the parade, too. Because I think at that time he was playing E-flat clarinet. I don't know whether he's playing E-flat, no, no.
He fell out, as he says, in the parade about four years ago. Oh, is that? The sun got him out, almost like a sunstroke. He hasn't played hardly a parade since.
Yeah, I remember him. And then too there's another fellow by the name of Humphrey. Yeah, Willie.
Willie Humphrey? Yeah, he still plays Paul Barber.
Yeah, well I think he come up later.
His father played too, back in the old Eagle Band 1910 to 1915 up there.
And there was somebody else down there, a very wonderful clarinet player.
You don't, no, you wouldn't remember George Bocquet?

No, I remember Peter, Peter Bocquet. Peter Bocquet. Peter Bocquet, I think he, I remember him, because I think at the time I left New Orleans he was President of the Union. But no, I don't remember Peter, the other fellow that played clarinet. But I remember an old trombone man back there, used to call him Jim Robinson I think, big,
tall, slender fellow. Yeah, yeah. He plays George Lewis. Oh yeah.
